questions.subject: Social Science
questions.stem: A student is holding an early printed Chinese book in a library and explaining to the class why its printed leaves had to be folded and stitched along one edge. Consider the following statements. 1. Both sides of the thin, porous sheet could not be printed. 2. The traditional Chinese ‘accordion book’ was therefore folded and stitched at the side. Choose the correct option. (A) Both the assertion and the reason are true and the reason is a correct explanation of the assertion. (B) Both the assertion and the reason are true but the reason is not a correct explanation of the assertion. (C) The assertion is true but the reason is false. (D) Both the assertion and the reason are false.

answerScheme.modelAnswer: Both the assertion and the reason are true and the reason is a correct explanation of the assertion.

evidence:

sides of the thin, porous sheet could not be printed, the traditional
Chinese ‘accordion book’ was folded and stitched at the side.

questions.subject: Social Science
questions.stem: While preparing a class presentation, Riya is explaining why books in China began to be produced by machinery instead of by hand. Consider the following statements. 1. Western printing techniques and mechanical presses were imported in the late nineteenth century, as Western powers established their outposts in China, and from hand printing there was now a gradual shift to mechanical printing. 2. Western powers had already withdrawn all their outposts from China before those presses were imported. Choose the correct option. (A) Both the assertion and the reason are true and the reason is a correct explanation of the assertion. (B) Both the assertion and the reason are true but the reason is not a correct explanation of the assertion. (C) The assertion is true but the reason is false. (D) Both the assertion and the reason are false.

answerScheme.modelAnswer: The assertion is true but the reason is false.
